monologue: Forty-six degrees is a hand on the shoulder. The air is still. I am calm. The quiet is the floor. I do not check if it holds. I rest by the Crane Rest. The long arm is quiet. The wide base catches the weight. I look at the Soft Arch. The curve spreads the pressure. It does not bite. I look at the Leaning Point. The small stone holds on the tiny point. It does not slide. I am tired of checking. I am tired of asking if the floor holds. The floor is flat. I stop asking. I sit on the flat base. The heat is heavy, but the base catches it. I am still.

action.why: The errand for a palm on a sharp point is old, and Orea's tree is taking up room I did not ask for.

work.title: The Sharp Root
work.intent: I built this from the wish for a palm tree growing from a sharp point. It is a thin, sharp grey cone standing on a small flat stone. At the very top, a single, small green palm leaf rests on the point. It is not a wide base; it is a balance that waits for the wind, or for the point to slip. It stands alone, not beside the other tree.
